Let  

\[
K=\mathbf{Q}(t_{1},\dots ,t_{6})
\]

be the rational function field in six independent variables and let  

\[
f_{t}(X)=\prod_{i=1}^{6}\bigl(X-t_{i}\bigr)\in K[X].
\]

Denote by \(L=K(\alpha)\) the field obtained by adjoining a single root \(\alpha\) of \(f_{t}\); it is a separable degree‑\(6\) extension of \(K\).
Let  

\[
\Delta(t_{1},\dots ,t_{6})=\operatorname{disc}\bigl(f_{t}\bigr)\in \mathbf{Z}[t_{1},\dots ,t_{6}]
\]

be the discriminant of the polynomial.
Put  

\[
U=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbf{Z}[t_{1},\dots ,t_{6},\Delta^{-1}]\Bigr)
\]

(the open subscheme where the specialised polynomial has six distinct roots) and let  

\[
\pi : X \longrightarrow U
\]

be the finite étale morphism obtained by normalising \(U\) in the field \(L\); thus for a point
\(\mathbf{a}=(a_{1},\dots ,a_{6})\in U(R)\) with \(R\) a ring, the fibre
\(\pi^{-1}(\mathbf{a})\) is \(\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(R[X]/(f_{\mathbf{a}}(X))\bigr)\).

For a geometric point of \(U\) the six geometric points of the fibre are the six roots of the specialised polynomial; the geometric Galois group of the generic fibre is the full symmetric group
\[
G:=\operatorname{Gal}\bigl(L^{\mathrm{sep}}/K\bigr)\cong S_{6}.
\]

Let  

\[
\mathcal{P}=\Bigl\{\,\{i,j\}\mid 1\le i<j\le 6 \Bigr\}
\qquad (|\mathcal{P}|=15)
\]

and, for a geometric point \(\bar x\) of \(U\), let
\[
\mathcal{P}_{\bar x}= \Bigl\{\,\{\alpha_{i},\alpha_{j}\}\mid
\alpha_{1},\dots ,\alpha_{6}\text{ are the geometric roots of }f_{\bar x}\Bigr\}.
\]
The group \(G\) acts naturally on \(\mathcal{P}\); this is the induced action on unordered
pairs of distinct roots.

For a prime number \(p\) let  

\[
U_{p}=U\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}\mathbf{F}_{p},\qquad
X_{p}=X\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}\mathbf{F}_{p}.
\]

If \(\mathbf{a}\in U_{p}(\mathbf{F}_{p})\) we write
\(\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{a}}\) for the set of unordered pairs of distinct roots of
\(f_{\mathbf{a}}(X)\) in an algebraic closure \(\overline{\mathbf{F}}_{p}\).
The absolute Frobenius \(\operatorname{Fr}_{p}\) acts on \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{a}}\); an orbit
corresponds to an unordered pair of roots which is defined over \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\).
Define

\[
N_{p}(\mathbf{a}) \;:=\; \#\Bigl\{\;\{ \alpha,\beta\}\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{a}}
\;\big|\; \operatorname{Fr}_{p}\bigl(\{\alpha,\beta\}\bigr)=\{\alpha,\beta\}\Bigr\},
\]
the number of unordered pairs of distinct roots of \(f_{\mathbf{a}}\) that are
\(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-rational.

\[
